newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Year of the Ox starts weak for Hong Kong stocks.
newsitem.headline: Year of the Ox starts weak for Hong Kong stocks.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks began the Year of the Ox on a weak note on Monday after an early rally fizzled throughout the session, but analysts said upcoming results announcements should invigorate the market.
The Hang Seng Index began the first trading day of the Chinese Lunar New Year with a surge of 196 points but ended the session down 16.96 points, or 0.12 percent, at 13,643.54.

"The Chinese thinking is that if things go well at the beginning of the year, it means that it is a good start so it is likely that the rest of the year will do very well," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
"If it closes higher it is a red opening and if it closes lower it is a black opening."

But the Year of the Rat also started on a weak note last year with a fall of 256.54 points, or 2.21 percent, in the Hang Seng. The blue-chip index went on to hit record highs during the course of the year.
"Certain Chinese traders like to play this game but I don't think there is any significance," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
He said the Hang Seng Index should reach the 14,000-point level once investors start to anticipate upcoming earnings reports.
"We continue to hold an optimistic outlook on both the property and banking sectors. With the announcement of results, this should help promote the rating of the market," he said.
Tsang said he had a mid-year target of 15,000 points, adding that the Hang Seng could test 14,000 either this week or next.
"There are really no major negatives for the market. It's close to the reporting season so people are buying stocks like HSBC ahead of the results announcement," he said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$5.50 on Monday to close at HK$189.50.
